title: CROP - LLM-powered VLSI design tuning via retrieval-augmented generation for parameter optimization
problem: VLSI design parameter optimization requires extensive manual tuning and domain expertise. Designers struggle to efficiently explore the large design space and apply best practices from past designs.
motivation: Leveraging LLMs with retrieval-augmented generation can automate parameter optimization by learning from historical design patterns and providing intelligent suggestions.
method: CROP retrieves similar successful circuit designs from past projects along with their design rules, providing this context to a large language model (LLM) to generate parameter recommendations. The recommended parameters are applied to the circuit, and their performance is measured against the design goals. Based on how well each recommendation worked, the LLM generates improved suggestions for the next iteration, and this cycle repeats until the design meets the performance targets.
key_novelty: The core contribution is using an LLM that learns from past successful circuit designs to automatically generate parameter recommendations, replacing the manual tuning experts normally do.
contributions: RAG-enhanced LLM framework for VLSI design parameter optimization
Methodology for retrieving and applying design patterns to new designs
limitations: The approach relies on the quality of historical design data and may not generalize to entirely novel design constraints or emerging technologies.
